original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.

actual_scope: Test a Pauli phase accumulator with explicit open/returned states, tensor and shared-bank implementations, and an actual two-type C/Q recursion through two levels.
scope_change_reason: The donor explicitly assigned a five-hour architectural investigation of underrepresented recursive boundary contracts after comparing three candidate directions. No random card was drawn. The connector-alphabet card records the closest family; this work does not extend its universal source-toggle query theorem.
bottleneck_link: The candidate must reduce a recursive supplier budget, not just named call count or scalar restoration. The concrete C/Q closure retains total child width; the support gate excludes width improvement by direct C/monomial refactoring. A successor needs a paid different mixing operation or a caller-compatible encoded endpoint.
stop_rule: Compare three mechanisms, select one, permit one bounded implementation pivot, test its smallest falsifying instance and two recursive levels. Stop construction when even the optimistic recursive moment is at least one; finish exact checks and a handoff without spending the remaining budget on a larger unchanged search.
evidence: README.md gives the all-size scoped representation and support arguments; RESULT.json records 23 full-column fixtures, 1692 forward columns, 559952 coefficients, a complete 512-column C9 inverse, all 512 nested live-bank open-state boundary columns, a 530-form binary census, 10 negative controls and paid finite program ledgers. INDEPENDENT.json uses separate Fraction/spectral and event-count implementations: all small fixtures, 12 columns each of C9 forward/inverse and nested bank open/returned boundaries. Same AI-assisted author; no independent human review, selected cold replay or new kappa.
author: Gareth Davidson (bitplane)
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in candidate comparison, derivation, proof drafting, code, exact replay and review. Both implementations have the same AI-assisted author. No sub-agents or independent human review.

open_questions.question: Can an actual caller consume a paid encoded boundary that changes the direct whole-array support gate?
open_questions.why_it_matters: C calls and monomial wrappers implementing the exact full output already need critical total child width; merely reordering their open states cannot create headroom.
open_questions.first_step: Pin one actual supplier call site and its accepted maps, specify the encoding and decoding, and test f=1,2 through two parent levels. Include all root transformations and reject the idea before a larger search if its complete relaxation cannot contract.
open_questions.blocked_by: No caller-compatible changed endpoint with a favorable paid implementation is established here.

open_questions.question: Can a different native mixing primitive implement the quadratic phase at a favorable completed price?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The support gate counts C-axis width, not the price of a genuinely different legal primitive; the explicit Q map supplies a small target and correctness control.
open_questions.first_step: Start from the explicit 4-by-4 Q1 kernel, identify a legal supplier operation outside the C/monomial product model, expand two levels, and charge the full operand volume, movement, precision and return before scaling up.
open_questions.blocked_by: A native implementation, its complete cost recurrence, and a link to the outer supplier contract remain missing.
